SUBJECT: CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP NO. 26-01) AND SITE PLAN AND
DESIGN REVIEW (PL NO. 26-0007)

PROJECT LOCATION/REQUEST:
Project Location: 10000 Atlantic Avenue
  o Assessor’s Parcel Numbers: 6221-011-036
  o Property Owner: Daniel Morales
  o Applicant: John Cataldo
  o Zoning: Light Manufacturing (M2)
  o Lot Size: 20,480 square feet, or 0.47 acres

Request: The applicant requests to change the use of the subject site from a truck dealership to
“green operation,” parking for a commercial fleet of box trucks, construction of a two-story office
and storage building, construction of a parking canopy, and other improvements. Per South Gate
Municipal Code (SGMC) Section 11.21.030, a CUP is required in the Light Manufacturing (M2)
zone for “renewable energy system, standalone or ground mounted” and “truck storage.”
Discretionary plan review is required for truck storage, and design review is required for
development on lots 15,000 square feet or more.

Required Permits
  • Conditional Use Permit (CUP No. 26-01) for “renewable energy system, standalone or
  ground mounted” and “truck storage.”
  • Site Plan and Design Review (PL No. 26-0007) for development of a site greater than
  15,000 SF.

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission:

  1. Find that in accordance with CEQA, this project qualifies for a categorical exemption under
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15332 (Class 32) “In-Fill Development Projects,” and is thereby
  exempt from CEQA in that urban uses surround the project site, and the project meets all
  other requirements to qualify for a Class 32 exemption.

  2. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-06 approving CUP No. 26-01 and PL No. 26-0007.

  9
 PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
The applicant requests approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to allow a “green operation”
parking lot for a commercial fleet of box trucks. The project site is located within the M2 (Heavy
Industrial) Zone and is subject to the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan.

The property is intended to be used by PacTrack, a logistics courier service that serves various
industries, including healthcare, legal, and government sectors. Electric charging stations will be
provided to charge box trucks while parked. Truck operations are expected to be conducted from
approximately 3:30 p.m. to 1:00 a.m. During operating hours, drivers will utilize the designated
truck parking spaces for personal vehicle parking while trucks are off-site. Upon return, trucks are
parked on-site for electric charging between approximately 1:00 a.m. and 3:30 p.m.

The office building will be staffed by one to two employees. The operation currently employs 12
drivers, with the potential to expand to up to 20 drivers based on the site layout.

The site is currently developed with an approximately 800-square-foot commercial office building
and has been used for truck sales. The proposed project would convert the existing use to a truck
parking facility designed to support regional operations. Proposed site improvements include:

  •  20 truck parking stalls
  o Employees will park personal vehicles in spaces when trucks are in use
  •  3 customer parking spaces
  •  Construction of a 2,274-square-foot (SF) building, including:
  o Retention of an existing 800 SF office space
  o Construction of an 844 SF second-floor addition
  o Construction of a 630 SF storage room
  •  Installation of a new on-site power station, including a battery energy storage system and
  charging stations
  •  Construction of an approximately 13,000 SF parking canopy spanning the entire parking
  area, equipped with solar panels
  •  Perimeter landscaping, fencing, and other improvements

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:
Under the California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et
seq., “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations §§
15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”), the project qualifies as a Class 32 Categorical Exemption
pursuant to Section 15332 (Class 32 – Infill Development Projects) of the CEQA Guidelines (Title
14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations).

BACKGROUND:

Site Location and Surroundings:
The site is flat, adequately sized, and capable of accommodating all required parking, circulation,
screening, and operational features. Two driveway access points are provided to facilitate
circulation and minimize traffic impacts.

The project site has access to Interstate 710 and is located west of Legacy High School, southeast
of Tweedy Elementary School and South Gate Park, and across from a vacant property at the

  10
 southwestern corner of Atlantic Avenue and Tweedy Boulevard. The surrounding area consists of
a mix of industrial, institutional, and emerging mixed-use development.

Consistency with Plans and Regulations:
The proposed use is consistent with the South Gate Municipal Code, the General Plan, and the
Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan. The project complies with applicable development standards
and incorporates site design and landscaping features to ensure compatibility with surrounding
uses.

The project incorporates sustainable elements, including a new power station and enhanced
landscaping, consistent with the City’s environmental and design objectives. Site improvements
are designed to provide appropriate screening and aesthetic integration with the surrounding area.

Project Overview
Site Characteristics: The subject site measures approximately 138 feet wide by 157 feet deep, and
is located at the northeastern corner of Atlantic Avenue and Chakemco Street. Table 1 provides a
summary of the lot dimensions and the lot area of the subject parcel, and Table 2 provides the

 ANALYSIS:

Required Findings for a CUP
Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be granted, the Planning Commission
(or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following findings, as applicable to the property:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose
  of this title or the city’s General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with
  the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to
  the character or function of the neighborhood.

1. Consistency with Zoning and General Plan: The proposed use is permitted subject to CUP
  approval and aligns with the intent of the M2 Zone and applicable planning documents.
2. Compatibility with Surrounding Uses: The project is designed to operate in a manner that is
  compatible with existing and future land uses in the vicinity.
3. Adequate Site Design: The site is sufficient in size and configuration to accommodate the
  proposed use, including parking, circulation, landscaping, and screening.
4. No Adverse Impacts: The project will not be detrimental to adjacent properties or the
  surrounding neighborhood due to its design, operational features, and traffic access provisions.
5. Public Convenience and Welfare: The project supports economic activity and provides a
  functional, sustainable commercial use that benefits the community.

The proposed Resolution supports the findings required under Section 11.52.030.

Issues of Concern

Parking
The site plan shows 20 truck parking spaces for box trucks that measure 10’ wide by 28’ deep.
Three customer (guest) spaces are provided, including one handicap space. The 2,274 SF building
is best categorized as a business office with 600 SF of ancillary storage. Based on the City’s
requirement of one parking space per 300 SF of gross floor area, eight parking spaces are required.
The applicant proposes that drivers use the truck parking spaces for their personal vehicles when
the trucks are off-site. When drivers return, the trucks will be parked overnight in those spaces.
This arrangement accommodates drivers’ personal vehicles and leaves three parking spaces
available for office staff and visitors. Although it is not ideal, this is an efficient way to utilize
parking spaces when trucks are off-site.

Additionally, the proposed 2,274 SF building is an expansion of an existing 800 SF building. There
are parking spaces currently provided; however, many of the spaces are used for parking trucks
for sale. The site currently has minimal landscaping, lighting, and other improvements. The
proposed project would improve these conditions.

  14
 Design/Site Plan Review
Development on parcels 15,000 square feet or larger is subject to Design Review and does not
require Planning Commission approval. Since the project includes a request for a Conditional Use
Permit (CUP), the project is being processed as a single, consolidated application. Pursuant to
SGMC Section 11.51.080, an application for a land use not permitted by right within a zone
requires a Site Plan Review for all project-related activities, subject to Planning Commission
approval.

Entrance to the site is from a 30-foot-wide driveway on Chakemco Street to the south. Vehicular
access is not provided onto Atlantic Avenue, although there will be a pedestrian walkway in the
northwestern corner of the site. A six-foot-high wrought-iron fence will be placed along the street
frontage with a 10-foot-wide landscape area between the fence and sidewalk. The landscaping will
soften views of the site from the public right-of-way and provide a buffer from pedestrians. A
condition has been included that the project meets the model water efficient landscape ordinance
(MWELO) requirements.

The applicant is proposing to expand an existing building and add a second floor. The building
will be rectangular and finished with smooth stucco. It will be located in the back corner where it
is least visible from the street. The parking canopy will cover much of the site and will be most
visible from the street. An architectural rendering has been provided showing a wavy roofline.
However, it is unlikely that the canopy would be built in this form due to the limited space for the
solar panels. The canopy will most likely be built flat, with a slight tilt toward the south to
maximize solar exposure.

A recycling area is located in the northeastern portion of the site next to the building. The recycling
area will need to be screened to meet Code. Any outdoor storage located behind the building along
the northern property line will have to be screened.

There are ample areas along the building and canopy to provide exterior lighting to provide better
security for the parking lot.

Conceptual signage has been provided on the renderings; however, final signage will be reviewed
and approved administratively to meet Code requirements.

Truck Parking and Circulation
The facility has the potential to serve 20 electric vehicle trucks. Recently, there have been concerns
with trucks operating in the City, particularly with the storage and parking of trucks. A traffic
report has been prepared for review by the Public Works Department, but after review, there are
concerns about the findings and recommended mitigation measures since the Public Works
Department has recently made street improvements to Chakemco Street. The Public Works
Department will continue to work with the applicant’s traffic engineer on appropriate measures.

Traffic is generally expected to head north and south along Atlantic Avenue. Access to the I-710
Freeway is available to the north on Firestone Boulevard, and to the south on Imperial Highway.
According to the traffic report, the proposed use is expected to generate substantially fewer vehicle
trips than the existing truck dealership use. The analysis shows that the net traffic impact of the
proposed project is minimal and will not create unsafe conditions on the surrounding street
network. The findings show that the project will generate 3 trips in AM and PM peak hours and
18 trips daily, which is below the County’s 100-trip threshold requiring a full Traffic Impact Study.

  15
 Proximity to Schools
Legacy High School and the International Studies Learning Center Middle School are located
about 1,000 feet to the east. Access is available on Tweedy Boulevard to the north, with secondary
access on Chakemco Street. Trucks leaving the site are expected to depart around 3:30 p.m., which
coincides with the end of the school day when kids leave. This may cause a traffic issue during
that time. However, since Chakemco Street is a secondary road that serves mostly industrial uses,
and traffic heading westbound on Chakemco Street must turn right at Atlantic Avenue, vehicles
coming from the schools are less likely to use Chakemco Street for egress.

Economic and Environmental Impacts
The proposed conversion of the site from a truck dealership to a “green” operation for parking
commercial box trucks presents both advantages and disadvantages. The existing dealership
generates sales tax revenue for the City, which would be largely lost with the proposed parking
use. With respect to traffic, the applicant’s analysis indicates that the proposed use may result in
fewer impacts than the current operation; however, the Public Works Department is still reviewing
these findings for accuracy.

The project would also provide several site improvements. The existing fence and landscaping
along Atlantic Avenue currently encroach into the public right-of-way; the proposal would correct
these conditions by providing a wider sidewalk and new landscaping, which greatly benefits the
area. In addition, the use of electric vehicles would support the adoption of cleaner technology
within the community.

Conclusion
Approval of the Conditional Use Permit and Site Plan and Design Review is justified as the project
is consistent with applicable regulations, compatible with surrounding uses, and will not result in
significant adverse impacts. The project represents an appropriate reuse of the site.

Effect of Signalized Intersection

The project driveway connects directly to Chakemco Street, approximately 50‑80 feet east of the
signalized intersection of Atlantic Avenue and Chakemco Street. At a fully signalized intersection
(like Atlantic & Chakemco), traffic on both the major (Atlantic) and minor (Chakemco) streets is
controlled by a traffic signal. This significantly reduces the risk of conflicts compared to an un-
signalized intersection, which is why some municipal codes recognize that sight distance
requirements are less restrictive at signalized intersections. The vehicle's movement is
governed by the signal phase, not solely by gap acceptance.

AASHTO sight distance guidelines are primarily intended for un-signalized intersections. For
driveways located near a signalized intersection, the signal provides protection, and the primary
requirement is corner clearance to prevent queue spillback into the intersection. As the strict
AASHTO sight distance requirements are often relaxed by municipal codes for driveways adjacent
to signalized intersections. However Vehicular Sight distance lines are added in the Internal
Circulation plan of the report. (See Annex-C)

Given the proposed use as a commercial fleet parking facility, truck movements will occur daily,
primarily during shift changes (early morning and late afternoon). To minimize conflicts between

area), several design and operational measures are recommended. The driveway entry and exit
points shall be clearly marked with “TRUCK ENTRANCE” and “TRUCK EXIT” signage, and
all trucks operating on site shall be equipped with audible backup alarms. The pedestrian crossing
at the driveway shall be controlled with high-visibility yield markings (ladder-style crosswalk) and
“YIELD TO PEDESTRIANS” warning signs. These measures, combined with the site’s low trip
generation (net decrease in daily trips), will ensure that pedestrian-truck conflicts remain
negligible.

Conclusion & Results

Below is a concise, section-by-section conclusion for the proposed fleet parking facility at 10000
Atlantic Avenue.

    Trip Generation- The existing truck sales use generates 3 AM, 4 PM, and 22 daily trips.
  The proposed fleet parking operation generates 3 AM, 3 PM, and 18 daily trips – a net
  reduction of 1 PM trips and 4 daily trips. The traffic impact is de minimis, and no full
  Traffic Impact Study is required.

    Queuing & Stacking- Maximum realistic queue is 2 vehicles, as peak hour trips are split
  between entering and exiting. With 90 feet of stacking depth and a 30-foot wide driveway,
  queues remain on-site and never spill back onto Chakemco Street or the signalized
  intersection.

    Sight Distance- AASHTO requires 490 feet of sight distance for a truck turning right, for
  a non-signalized intersection. After removing existing encroachments, the available
  distance exceeds this requirement. The signalized intersection further reduces risk, and a
  36-inch convex mirror is recommended as an additional safety enhancement.

    Internal Circulation & Maneuvering- AutoTURN simulations confirm that all design
  vehicles (box trucks, delivery trucks, refuse trucks) can safely enter, circulate, and exit
  using 30-foot aisles, 10 ft × 28 ft fleet stalls, and a designated trash enclosure.

    Multimodal Access- A full-width ADA sidewalk will replace existing encroachments.
  Detectable warning surfaces, a high-visibility crosswalk, bicycle racks, and continued
  access to bus stops ensure full compliance with City requirements.

    Potential Safety Concerns- Six concerns (sight distance, queue spillback,
  pedestrian-truck conflicts, turning radii, corner clearance, wrong-way entry, ADA
  compliance) are identified and each is addressed by specific mitigation measures. No
  unresolved safety issues remain.

    Recommended Mitigation Measures- Remove all ROW encroachments; install a 36-inch
  convex mirror; provide 90 ft stacking depth and 30-ft driveway; add “USE BOTH LANES”
  signage, directional arrows, and “TRUCK ENTRANCE/EXIT” signs; install
  high-visibility crosswalk, “YIELD TO PEDESTRIANS” signs, speed bumps, and backup
  alarms; construct ADA sidewalk with detectable warnings; provide bicycle racks. These
  measures satisfy all Conditions of Approval.

 ANALYSIS: On February 5, 2026, the applicant Lorena Melendez (Business Owner), on behalf
of Niky’s Sports, Inc., submitted a request to paint a mural on the western exterior wall of the
business, which would be visible to pedestrian and vehicular traffic traveling east on Tweedy
Boulevard. The mural shall be removed no later than January 31, 2027.

Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Chapter 11.36.090, “any painted wall sign that does not
pertain to the business, product, or service rendered on the premises shall be considered a mural.
Size, height, and other restrictions shall be reviewed by the Planning Commission.”

South Gate is a diverse, vibrant community powered by minorities, families, and generations of
people who take pride in where they live. Football – soccer – is a global game that transcends
language, background, and borders, and it plays a meaningful role in bringing people together
across cultures. According to the applicant, this mural is intended to celebrate that shared
connection. By highlighting the world’s game, the project reflects the identity of South Gate as a
community rooted in unity, passion, and resilience. Art has the power to uplift neighborhoods,
create shared memories, and inspire younger generations. This mural is meant to be something that
the South Gate community can remember, take ownership of, and feel proud of.

The mural would measure approximately 58’-6” in length and 16’-3” in height. The muralist is
Sebastian Oyarbide, an Argentine native, whose work has taken him around the world. His artistic
practice is deeply influenced by movement, culture, and the environments he inhabits. Through
murals and large-scale public works, Sebastian seeks to create visual narratives that connect people
to place and to one another. Growing up in Argentina, soccer was an ever-present part of daily
life- more than a sport, it was a shared language that united communities across backgrounds and
generations. Los Angeles has become an important source of inspiration for Sebastian. As a city
defined by diversity, creativity, and cultural exchange, LA reflects many of the same values that
soccer represents worldwide. Through his mural in South Gate, Sebastian hopes to express his love
for both the world’s game and the city where he practices his art – creating a piece that resonates
with the local community while honoring the universal spirit of soccer. By contributing this mural,
Sebastian aims to give back to the community through art that is accessible, inclusive, and
reflective of the people who live there.

the activity will have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual circumstances. The
property is already developed, and the proposed use is for the painting of a mural on the exterior
